Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about the performance profile you showed. Procurement asked me to get ahead of sequencing so we don't run into last‑minute legal blockers. Two primary asks from our side:

1) Can you draft a mutual action plan that aligns the technical evaluation milestones with the MSA/DPA review and the order form sign-off? We need visibility on what can run in parallel and what must be serial.
2) We need proposed acceptance windows and ownership for each checkpoint (security review, SOC 2 evidence, pilot acceptance, commercial sign-off). Our legal counsel flagged the DPA review as a potential two‑week blocker depending on redlines.

I've attached our RFP and a short procurement checklist. Happy to host a 30‑minute alignment call.

Subject: Re: Sequencing questions for Redwood pilot (signature ladder / acceptance windows)

Elena — thanks for sending. Drafted a concise MAP that ties the eval checkpoints to legal/procurement gates and highlighted which items can be parallelized. Key points up front:

- Parallelizable: DPA review (legal) + technical pilot (security evidence collection) — we can run these simultaneously provided your security team gives access to the eval prompt set within 2 business days.
- Serial: MSA redlines need resolution before we finalize the order form. Order form must reference the agreed SLAs and billing cadence.
- Signature ladder: Legal (orion legal) -> Procurement -> Finance (CFO) -> Exec sponsor sign-off. We recommend a staged signature (MSA + DPA countersigned, then order form countersigned).

I attached an initial MAP spreadsheet (initial-map-draft.xlsx) with suggested owners, target days-to-complete, and contingency buffers. High-level timeline suggestion:
  Week 0: Kickoff & access to eval environment
  Week 0–2: Technical pilot + DPA review (parallel)
  Week 2–3: MSA redline cycle + order form alignment (serial)
  Week 3–4: Final redlines, signoffs, and DocuSign routing

Outstanding asks from our side: confirm the orion legal reviewer for DPA (name/email) and the procurement lead who will own the PO submission. Also, please confirm whether data residency controls require on‑prem footprint (that changes DPA scope).

If helpful, I can book a 30‑minute slot tomorrow to walk through the MAP and acceptance criteria.

Attachments: initial-map-draft.xlsx

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer

Adding a few practical notes from the legal/orderform perspective:

- Order form dependency: we need the commercial terms (billing cadence, seat counts, committed throughput) to be agreed before we populate the order form. If procurement wants to reserve dedicated capacity, that will add a short legal addendum and potentially extend order form completion by ~3 business days.
- Acceptance criteria: recommend a two‑step acceptance (pilot acceptance by product/engineering + compliance acceptance by security/legal). Pilot acceptance should be gated on latency/throughput thresholds we ran in the demo; I'll add suggested numeric thresholds to the MAP.
- Pricing owner: CC'd Rishi for cadence on committed capacity pricing and any CRO approval steps.

Happy to review the MAP tomorrow; suggest we confirm the legal and finance approvers so DocuSign routing can be configured in advance.

—Laura Bennett

Thanks — this is exactly the clarity we needed. Quick decisions from our side:

- DPA reviewer: Elena legal counsel (Elena.Legal@orionhealth.com) — she'll own redline consolidation.
- Procurement lead: Mark Chen <mark.chen@orionhealth.com> — he'll manage PO timing and whether we elect dedicated capacity.
- Data residency: no on‑prem required for pilot; we will include a scoped data residency clause in the DPA for production only.

We're good to proceed with the parallel DPA + technical pilot plan. Please:
  1) Share the MAP with the added numeric acceptance thresholds (Laura mentioned)
  2) Add DocuSign routing placeholders for the signature ladder you recommend
  3) Send a calendar invite for a 30‑minute kickoff tomorrow at 11:00 PT to confirm owners and kickoff artifacts.
